sources.locator: HTML Living Standard; living standard accessed 2026-07; provisions applicable to Comments and character references
sources.claim: HTML comments annotate source without becoming rendered text, while character references represent characters that would otherwise be syntax or hard to type.

canonicalExplanation.summary: Some characters mean something to the HTML parser: `<` starts a tag and `&` starts a **character reference**. To show them as plain text, write `<` and `&` (and `>` for >, `"` inside attribute quotes). **Comments** `<!-- … -->` are hidden on the page but **fully visible** in View Source — never put secrets, keys or private notes in them.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
You're writing a tutorial page that says "wrap code in the <code> element". The sentence vanishes halfway, and the rest of the page turns monospace! The browser read `<code>` as a real tag. The source writes <code> to display literal angle brackets instead of creating a code element. In this lesson you'll repair text that is accidentally parsed as markup and remove misleading commented-out secrets.

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: You should know **Elements, attributes and nesting** — which characters start tags and attributes.

sections.heading: The rule: escape characters the parser treats as markup

sections.heading: Comments are public notes

includes: Escape <, & and quotes so text isn't parsed as markup.
Use comments only for harmless notes and remove secrets from markup.

outcomes: Repair text that is accidentally parsed as markup and remove misleading commented-out secrets.

examples.title: Showing <code> on the page
examples.situation: The source writes <code> to display literal angle brackets instead of creating a code element.
walkthrough: **Problem:** `Wrap code in the <code> element.` — the parser opens a real code element and the rest turns monospace.
**Result:** the browser parses the references and displays literal angle brackets, and no code element is created.
examples.result: The page shows "Wrap code in the <code> element." as plain text, and the rest of the page looks normal.

examples.title: The commented-out config
examples.situation: A developer comments out old markup: `<!-- <script>const KEY = "sk_live_9f…"</script> -->` to "disable" it.
walkthrough: The script no longer runs, but the comment and the key are still sent to every visitor.
Anyone can copy the key from View Source.
Fix: delete the block entirely, revoke the leaked key, and keep secrets on the server.
examples.result: No secret remains in the page source, and the exposed key can no longer be used.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: HTML comments are private and safe for API keys because browsers do not display them.
misconceptions.correction: Comments are delivered to every visitor and visible in View Source and DevTools; they're only hidden from the rendered page. Secrets must never appear in HTML — delete them and revoke any leaked key.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "The commented-out config", why wasn't commenting out enough?

analogy.example: Character references are like **quoting someone's words** in writing: you put quotes around "stop" so readers know it's a word, not an instruction. Comments are like **pencil notes in a library book** — the next reader sees them too.
usefulFor: remembering escaping = "this is text, not a command"
remembering comments travel with the page
limitations: Pencil can be erased; comments stay until you delete them from the source.
The parser recognises only specific references, like < and &.

steps.explanation: The source writes character references instead of raw angle brackets.
Because the brackets are escaped, the parser does not create a code element.
The browser displays literal angle brackets as plain text.

trace.textAlternative: Displaying markup characters as text. Step 1, Read references: < is <; > is >. The source writes character references instead of raw angle brackets. remediation.explanation: Before publishing, search your HTML for `<!--` and read every comment as if a stranger will — because one will. Then search visible text for `<` and `&` and escape them.

recap.summary: To repair text that is accidentally parsed as markup, escape < as <, & as & and quotes inside attributes as ". Comments are public: remove misleading commented-out secrets from the source entirely and revoke any that leaked.
